questions.question: Define amplitude, wavelength, period and frequency, giving the SI unit of each, and explain what a transverse wave transfers.
questions.expected_answer: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of a particle of the medium from its equilibrium (rest) position, measured in metres — not the crest-to-trough distance, which is two amplitudes. Wavelength is the distance between two successive points in phase, such as crest to next crest, also measured in metres. The period is the time taken for one complete wave to pass a fixed point, measured in seconds. Frequency is the number of complete waves passing a fixed point per second, measured in hertz. A transverse wave transfers energy through the medium without transferring matter: the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of travel and return to their rest positions.

questions.question: A ripple tank vibrator runs at 20 Hz and produces ripples of wavelength 3 cm. Calculate the wave speed and the period, showing formula, substitution and answer with units.
questions.expected_answer: Speed: v = fλ. Convert the wavelength first, since 3 cm = 0,03 m. Substituting, v = (20)(0,03) = 0,6 m·s⁻¹. Period: T = 1/f = 1 ÷ 20 = 0,05 s. Each line must appear — the formula, the substitution with converted SI units, and the answer with its unit — because the memo awards marks separately for each. The check on the answer is that hertz multiplied by metres gives metres per second, which is a speed, so the units confirm the working.

questions.question: Explain why shaking a rope faster does not make the wave travel faster, and describe how to tell from a graph whether you are measuring a wavelength or a period.
questions.expected_answer: Wave speed is determined by the properties of the medium — the tension and mass of the rope, or the depth of the water — not by the source. Shaking faster raises the frequency, and because v = fλ with v fixed, the wavelength shortens in exact proportion so that the product stays the same. Frequency is set by the source, speed by the medium, and wavelength is what adjusts. On a graph the horizontal axis decides the reading: displacement versus position is a snapshot of the wave along the medium, so the repeating distance is the wavelength; displacement versus time follows one particle oscillating, so the repeating interval is the period. The two graphs look identical, so the axis label must be read before any measurement is taken.
